_comment: Ceilings for how far this backend may differ from the committed (WebGL2-blessed) references. A LIST OF DEBTS, not of blessings: every entry is an undiagnosed WebGPU-vs-WebGL2 disagreement. The gate fails when a frame exceeds its ceiling, or when an unlisted frame exceeds the tolerance. Entries are meant to be removed; run.mjs names the ones that have improved enough to tighten.

_notes.glass-grain#0: RAISED BY HAND 2026-08-12, 0.32183 -> 0.32712, cause UNATTRIBUTED. Measured at 32.712% in six independent process launches; the 0.32183 ceiling came from a single sample taken when this file was first written. Four hypotheses were tested and eliminated by re-rendering: scene order (removed the two new extrusion scenes), the MASK_TARGET orphan skip, the BEAM shader registration, and the twelve one-sided shading edits. The changes left are WebGL2-only code or a field never set for glass, and the WebGL2 reference comparison never moved. So this is either a one-sample baseline that was low, or a real change nobody has found. Raised rather than swept by --update-backend-baseline so it stays a named debt with its evidence attached.
_notes.effect-compound-blur#0: NARROWED 2026-08-12, not fixed. The three scenes reading ANOTHER LAYER as a map -- compound-blur 53.3%, displacement-map-layer 19.8%, displacement-map 15.8% -- are the ONLY scenes that do so, and all three diverge on WebGPU. They share displacementMapTexture(), which renders the map into MATTE_TARGET via renderableCmds. ELIMINATED, do not re-check: (1) the shader arithmetic -- compound-blur WGSL and GLSL are character-identical, and reverting the one-sided shading edits left the divergence unchanged; (2) map ORIENTATION and (3) surface-format CHANNEL ORDER -- compound-blur map is a full-comp horizontal BLACK-TO-WHITE greyscale ramp, which is invariant under a V-flip and under BGRA/RGBA swap, so neither can move its radius field. LIVE HYPOTHESIS: the map ALPHA. The shader reads mapC.rgb WITHOUT dividing by alpha (deliberately -- see its comment), so on a premultiplied MATTE_TARGET the rgb it reads is already alpha-scaled. MATTE_TARGET is cleared TRANSPARENT and the map drawn into it; if the two backends end with different alpha there, lum and therefore the radius scale differently -- which matches the symptom, a WEAKER blur on WebGPU at the bright end. Next step: read back MATTE_TARGET alpha on both backends for effect-compound-blur.
